architecture.title: AI-Q Open Agent Blueprint — route → plan → fan out → tools
architecture.caption: A cheap Nemotron Nano router answers shallow queries directly and escalates hard ones to a Deep Agent, which writes an explicit plan and fans out parallel researcher sub-agents over the NeMo Agent Toolkit tool bus. Route small, escalate rarely, fan out in parallel — that routing decision is the ~50%-cost lever.

charts.title: Routing economics on a 6-query mix
charts.caption: labs/lab01_router_economics.py: with a deep run ≈ 9× a shallow answer and 3 of 6 queries staying shallow, blended cost drops 9.0 → 5.0 units (~44% saved). NVIDIA's '~50% cheaper' claim is exactly this math on THEIR workload mix — swap in your queries and the saving is your number.

charts.title: Researcher fan-out — sum of latencies vs wall clock
charts.caption: labs/lab02_plan_fanout.py sample trace: A ~6.1 s + B ~6.8 s of research finish in ~6.9 s of wall clock — a ~1.9× fan-out speedup. Your numbers vary with the endpoint; single-instance Ollama can serialize to ~1.0×.

charts.title: Query mix behind the saving
charts.caption: The lab01 QUERIES set: 3 lookups ('Who founded NVIDIA?', Ollama's port, Spark memory) stay shallow; 3 multi-step questions (TCO comparison, on-prem legal research, routing analysis) go deep. The saving depends entirely on this ratio.
